Open Curator's Vault: Classics. Review Terms and Privacy — both tabs — then Accept.
Swipe the welcome slides. Identify a piece, keep a private vault, and hunt grails on eBay.
On the last slide, tap Get Started.
If it asks what to call you, type a name or skip. You can change it later in Settings.
Pick the types you care about: coins, paper money, trading cards, stamps, and lighters. Comics are not on this list.
Tap Explore with a sample vault if you want a demo collection first.
Or skip samples and start empty — you can Identify or add a piece anytime.
When sample data is on, a banner reminds you these are demo pieces.
Tap Clear samples when you are ready for your own vault.
You land on Home. The status line shows how many pieces are in the vault and on your wish list.
The bottom bar has four tabs: Home, My Collection, Tools, and Settings.
Tap Identify a piece — the recommended path — or tap Identify on the command row.
Add to my vault opens Collection so you can type a piece in yourself.
Hunt a grail opens your wish list. Verify a cert tracks slab numbers.
Tap Identify. Choose Coin, Paper Money, Trading Card, Stamp, or Lighter.
Lay the piece flat and keep it fully in frame. One still photo is enough.
Tap Take Photo, or Choose Photo for a picture you already have.
What you already know is optional. Add a date, mint mark, or catalog number only if you have it.
Tap Identify when you have a photo. You can leave the other fields blank.
The report names the piece. If the top match is wrong, check the other possibilities.
Current asking range is from similar active listings — asking prices, not solds.
If a coin is flagged Scan individually, photograph that one by itself, laid flat, then Identify again.
Scan individually is not a sold price.
Tap Save to Vault. The piece lands in My Collection with the photo and details filled in.
Identify history keeps past reports. Open it from Identify or from Tools.
With no signal, Curator's Vault queues the job and runs it when you reconnect. Watch the banner on Home.
Tap the My Collection tab — briefcase, second from the left.
Owned is what you have. Wish is what you are hunting. For Sale is what you are selling.
Tap a row to open the piece — photos, grade, provenance, and value.
On the piece, add notes, purchase price, and service or restoration when you have them.
Swipe Manage your vault for Timeline, Insights, Portfolio P&L, Buying budget, Inventory, Insurance, and Grail Radar.
To add without a photo, tap Add and enter the details yourself. Save. It is in Owned right away.
Open Portfolio P&L for cost, estimated value, and gain or loss across the vault.
Buying budget tracks spend against a monthly or yearly cap from the purchase prices you enter.
Insurance report builds a photo-and-value packet for a policy. Inventory report is the printable list.
Tap Wish, then add a grail — type, keywords, and a max you will pay.
Open that wish row's Grail Radar. Set hunt rules and tap Save.
Tap Check now. Matches show title, asking price, and a link.
Any match opens the eBay listing in your browser.
When a new match lands, a notification jumps you back to that grail.
From Tools, eBay listings searches active comps by what you type — asking, not a solds feed.
Price alerts and Flea markets watch targets the same way. Trade analyzer compares two pieces before you swap.
Tap Compare on Tools. Pick two vault items for side-by-side photos and specs.
Tap the Tools tab. On the floor is the show-floor row: Web companion, Barcode, Compare, Share, and Inventory.
Identify, Identify history, and Estate intake sit under Identify.
Estate intake is for a box of pieces — photograph and catalog them one at a time.
Under Authenticate, open Grading guide for condition language. Condition walks a checklist on a piece.
Cert tracker stores PCGS, PSA, and other cert numbers. Zippo decoder reads a lighter bottom stamp.
Set completion shows what you still need in a set you are building.
Photo studio, Barcode scanner, and Document scanner attach pictures, UPCs, and paperwork to a piece.
AI chat answers collector questions. Collectible passport is a proof card with photos and key facts.
Event calendar and Display rotation help you plan shows and what sits out.
Offline viewing keeps a pack on the phone when you will have no signal.
Tap Web companion, then Start. The phone shows a local address and a large four-digit code.
On a PC on the same Wi-Fi, open that address and type the code. Changes sync back to the phone.
Share and connect sends a piece or a want list nearby. PIN is on the phone; Bluetooth is optional.
Tap Settings — gear at the bottom right.
Language switches the display. Eight languages ship in this version.
Privacy explains what leaves the phone when you Identify. Export is in that screen.
File backup: Save a Copy to Drive, Files, or email. Bring a Copy Back on another phone and confirm before it replaces data.
Security and App Lock uses your device biometrics or passcode. Canceling leaves the vault locked.
Curator's Vault includes a 14-day Pro trial from first open — no card. Reinstall on this phone does not restart the clock.
After the trial, Upgrade in Settings is monthly or yearly through Google Play or the App Store.
Questions? Use Send feedback in Settings, or email support@josspatech.com.
This user guide lives at josspatech.com/videos/cvc/user-guide — same address the Help row opens.
